figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Natural and artificial pathways from baccatin III to Taxol. (a) The native pathway converts baccatin III to Taxol through five enzymatic
reactions, in which PAM activity is barely detectable in yeast. (b) The hypothesized artificial pathway bypasses the C2′ oxidation and β-
phenylalanine isomerization steps and requires only three enzymatic reactions. Abbreviations not already defined in the text are as follows: PAM,
phenylalanine aminomutase; PCL, β-phenylalanoyl-CoA ligase; BAPT, baccatin III:3-amino-3-phenylpropanoyltransferase; T2′OGD, taxoid-2′-
oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase; T3′NBT, taxoid-3′-N-benzoyltransferase; AAE4, benzoyl-CoA ligase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Functional characterization of key enzymes PAMs and PCLs in yeast. (a) PAMs were individually expressed in yeast strain BTP2-1
harboring the downstream pathway genes, and their enzymatic activities were evaluated by monitoring the accumulation of 3′-N-debenzoyl-2′-
deoxytaxol following feeding with β-phenylalanine or L-phenylalanine. (b) Catalytic activities of PCLs from different species toward the native
substrate β-phenylalanine or the non-native substrate (2R,3S)-3-phenylisoserine were assessed by coexpression with BAPT and quantification of the
accumulation of 3′-N-debenzoyl-2′-deoxytaxol or 3′-N-debenzoyltaxol. Different colors denote distinct taxane products: yellow, 3′-N-debenzoyl-2′-
deoxytaxol; green, 3′-N-debenzoyltaxol. Data are presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Favorable binding poses ofTmeBAPT with the substrates β-phenylalanoyl-CoA and baccatin III and protein engineering to enhance
activity toward the non-native substrate (2R,3S)-3-phenylisoserinoyl-CoA. (a) Schematic representation of residues located within 4 Å of the β-
phenylalanoyl side chain, including F43, M384, L385, Q386, Q387, L394, P395, Y397, and F416, shown in pink, with Q386 highlighted in purple.
(b) Q386 and neighboring residues Q387 and Q388 are positioned close to the carbonyl and amino groups of the β-phenylalanoyl moiety in
TmeBAPT and may form hydrogen bonds with the substrate. The surfaces of residues Q386, Q387, and Q388 are highlighted in cyan. β-
Phenylalanoyl-CoA is shown in green, and the structure of TmeBAPT is shown in gray. (c) Activities of TmeBAPT mutants at positions Q386,
Q387, and Q388 toward the non-native substrate (2R,3S)-3-phenylisoserinoyl-CoA were characterized by coexpression with TchPCL in yeast and
quantification of 3′-N-debenzoyltaxol production. (d) Combination mutants of Q386, Q387, and Q388 were further evaluated using the same
approach; however, none outperformed the Q386E single mutant. Data are presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples).
Statistical significance was assessed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s multiple-comparisons test.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Whole-cell conversion of baccatin III to Taxol. (a) Representative chromatograms of heterologous Taxol production in strains harboring
either the artificial pathway or the native pathway genes, validating the functions of TcaDBTNBT and TchT3′NBT. (b) Quantification of Taxol
accumulation in strains carrying the artificial or native pathway, determined by LC−QQQ MS analysis. (c) Representative chromatograms showing
the accumulation of 2′-deoxytaxol in native-pathway strains lacking T2′OGD, in order to define the substrate scope of TcaDBTNBT. (d)
Quantification of 2′-deoxytaxol accumulation in native-pathway strains lacking T2′OGD, determined by LC−QQQ MS analysis. Different colors
denote distinct taxane products: purple, 2′-deoxytaxol and pink, Taxol. Data are presented as mean ± s.d. (n = 3 biologically independent samples).
